props.name: poisoned catalysts may be regenerated

evidence.quote: When, through poisoning, these catalysts, become less efficient, they may be - regenerated either by heating to 800-400° C. 15 ina current of air or oxygen, or by dissolving up in sulphuric acid and reprecipitating the complex carbonates with soda ash.

props.statement: When through poisoning the catalysts become less efficient, they may be regenerated by heating in a current of air or oxygen, or by dissolving in sulphuric acid and reprecipitating the complex carbonates with soda ash.

props.name: Example 1: chromate reduced by zinc, precipitated with soda ash

evidence.quote: A strong solution of sodium bichromate or chromate is mixed with sulphuric acid —_ and the hot mixture (90° C.) is heated with g granulated zinc metal to effect reduction of the bichromate to chromium sulphate.

When the reduction is finished a solution of soda ash (5-10 per cent excess) 1s added; the pre- cipitate thrown down consists of a mixture of 65 basic zinc and chromium carbonates, which is separated, washed well with hot water and dried.
Itis then made into pellets and intro- duced. into the catalytic apparatus.
Iprefer _ to proportion the zinc and chromium so that +. | the precipitate contains 70-80 moles of zinc to 380-20 moles of chromium.
the amount of zinc may not be sufficient to effect reduction of all the chromium and addi- - tion reducing agents may then be used

props.method: reduction of sodium bichromate or chromate in sulphuric acid with granulated zinc at 90 °C to chromium sulphate; precipitation of the basic zinc and chromium carbonates with soda ash; washing, drying, pelleting
steps: a strong solution of sodium bichromate or chromate is mixed with sulphuric acid and the hot mixture (90° C.) is heated with granulated zinc metal to reduce the bichromate to chromium sulphate
a solution of soda ash (5-10 per cent excess) is added; the precipitate is a mixture of basic zinc and chromium carbonates
the precipitate is separated, washed well with hot water and dried
it is made into pellets and introduced into the catalytic apparatus

temperature.note: the hot mixture during reduction with zinc

props.name: Example 2: bichromate reduced in a zinc-carbon cell, precipitated with soda ash

evidence.quote: A solution of bichromate in aqueous sul- phuric acid is placed as electrolyte in a cell. having a zinc negative pole and a carbon positive pole.

By taking current from the cell the bichromate is reduced and the spent electrolyte eventually contains the requisite amount of zinc and chromium sulphate for or the precipitation with soda ash, which follows | as before.
The zinc o5 electrode may also be amalgamated to pre- vent. direct attack by the acid.

props.method: bichromate in aqueous sulphuric acid as electrolyte of a cell with zinc negative pole and carbon positive pole; current taken from the cell reduces the bichromate; the spent electrolyte (zinc and chromium sulphate) is precipitated with soda ash as in Example 1
steps: a solution of bichromate in aqueous sulphuric acid is the electrolyte of a cell with a zinc negative pole and a carbon positive pole
current is taken from the cell until the spent electrolyte contains the requisite zinc and chromium sulphate
precipitation with soda ash follows as in Example 1
the zinc electrode may be amalgamated to prevent direct attack by the acid
